description: From Dakar, Senegal, tackling the MODIS/VIIRS hotspot harmonization challenge. Every dry season, bushfires and agricultural burns sweep across the Sahel, but the satellite fire record is split across sensors that can't be compared directly. My goal is to build a web app that merges 20+ years of fire data into a clear "burning calendar," ..
summary: FireSync Sahel is a free, bilingual (French/English) web platform that turns 25 years of NASA satellite fire observations into decisions for bushfire management in Senegal and The Gambia. Every dry season, nearly a quarter of Senegal burns, destroying grazing land, soils and forests. NASA has observed every fire since 2000, but the older (MODIS) and newer (VIIRS) sensors do not see the same fires: simply joining them creates a false three-fold "explosion" of fires in 2012. FireSync uses machine learning to harmonise MODIS, VIIRS S-NPP, NOAA-20 and NOAA-21 detections into one consistent weekly fire calendar for any area, a district, a classified forest or a hand-drawn zone validated by holding out entire years (21% error per area and week, versus 73% without correction). A second AI model forecasts the next 4 weeks for all 93 districts, ranks where to act first and drafts a ready-to-send SMS/WhatsApp alert for village fire committees, with printable PDF bulletins. Every number is explained in plain language. The method works anywhere NASA FIRMS has data.
details:
FIRESYNC SAHEL – FROM SATELLITE OBSERVATION TO A VILLAGE ALERT

Live platform (free, French/English, desktop and mobile): https://firesyncsahel.vercel.app

THE PROBLEM

Every dry season, nearly a quarter of Senegal (about 4.4 million hectares) burns. In Kédougou, more than a third of the district burns every year. In 2024-25, about 6 million tonnes of fodder went up in smoke (≈499 billion CFA francs), weakening livestock and food self-sufficiency. NASA satellites have recorded every fire since 2000, but the record is hard to use: MODIS (Terra, Aqua) and VIIRS (Suomi NPP, NOAA-20, NOAA-21) detect different numbers of fires, so a naive merge shows a false ×3.3 jump in 2012. And no tool tells forest services and village committees where to act next week.

WHAT IT DOES

1. A harmonised fire calendar for any area: pick a district, draw a polygon or upload a GeoJSON (classified forest, grazing corridor…) and get 25 seasons week by week – onset, peak, end, critical weeks, abnormal years, 25-year trend and where the current season stands against history.

2. An AI forecast 1 to 4 weeks ahead for the 93 districts of Senegal and The Gambia: expected fires with a 90% range, a risk level and a "where to act first" ranking.

3. A ready-to-send SMS/WhatsApp alert in French or English for fire committees and village chiefs, bilingual PDF bulletins and CSV/GeoJSON exports.

4. Plain-language explanations of every number ("busier than in 80% of past seasons", "about 1 chance in 4"), so non-specialists can act on them.

5. Public, professional (followed zones, alert thresholds) and administrator spaces.

HOW IT WORKS

- NASA data: FIRMS active fires (MODIS C6.1 and VIIRS 375 m from S-NPP, NOAA-20 and NOAA-21), archive and near real time; MODIS land cover (MCD12Q1) to adapt the correction to the landscape; MODIS burned area (MCD64A1) as an independent check; MODIS NDVI (MOD13A1) tested as a fuel indicator.

- Detections are cleaned and aggregated weekly on an H3 hexagonal grid.

- A Poisson gradient-boosting ensemble learns how to convert MODIS detections into VIIRS S-NPP equivalents, cell by cell, season by season and by land cover, using matched Aqua/S-NPP overpasses (±60 min). NOAA-20 and NOAA-21 are also converted to S-NPP equivalents, so the record continues after the end of Suomi NPP data distribution.

- Validation by holding out entire fire years: 21% error per area and week versus 73% for a naive merge; the 2012 jump in the detections/burned-area ratio drops from ×3.32 to ×1.04; the 90% intervals contain the true value 9 times out of 10.

- A second gradient-boosting model forecasts the next 4 weeks from the seasonal normal, recent activity and its anomaly, the season-to-date total, the previous season, the neighbourhood and land cover. Probabilities are calibrated year by year. Tested on 12 held-out seasons (2013–2024): 9.7% more accurate than the seasonal normal, AUC 0.65. An ablation study showed that NDVI did not improve the forecast, so it was left out – and the result is published on the platform.

IMPACT

In Senegal, forest services and village fire committees can plan firebreaks, early burns and patrols 2 to 4 weeks ahead, protect dry-season grazing and classified forests, and decide on consistent data. Avoiding just 1% of the 2024-25 fodder losses would save about 5 billion CFA francs in a single season. Worldwide, moving to another country is a configuration change: FireSync can run anywhere NASA FIRMS has data (the whole Sahel, the Amazon, the Mediterranean). It supports SDG 2 (Zero hunger), SDG 13 (Climate action) and SDG 15 (Life on land).

TOOLS

Python (polars, scikit-learn, H3, shapely, matplotlib, ReportLab), FastAPI, plain JavaScript with MapLibre, deck.gl and Observable Plot, SQLite locally and Postgres online, hosted on Vercel, code on GitHub. 62 automated tests, including checks of our statistics against reference implementations.

WHAT MAKES IT CREATIVE

- Sensor harmonisation at the scale of a 250 km² cell, with an uncertainty that is validated, not assumed.

- Forecasts published together with their measured skill, calibration curve and ablation study.

- Outputs that speak the language of the field: a text message ready to forward, not only charts.

- Every indicator translated into a plain sentence, in French and English.

FACTORS WE CONSIDERED

- Honesty: every value comes with a validated range; the model's skill and limits are shown (it does not yet use weather data; satellites miss fires under clouds or very small fires).

- No false alarms: a "high risk" level needs both an abnormal ratio and a meaningful number of fires.

- Field use: bilingual, mobile-friendly, light pages served from a CDN for low bandwidth.

- Continuity of NASA data after Suomi NPP, through NOAA-20 and NOAA-21.

- Security: hashed passwords, signed sessions, no secrets in the code.

TEAM

Papa Seydou WANE (@papaseydouwane) and Berthe Diatta Diaite – Senegal.

All results come from NASA and partner data processed by our code, and were checked through held-out-year validation and automated tests. The narration of the video is a synthetic voice generated offline with the open-source Kokoro text-to-speech model. Charts and maps are drawn by our code from the data; no image was made with an image-generation model, and no NASA logo was generated or modified.

FireSync Sahel is not an official NASA product. We acknowledge the use of data and imagery from LANCE FIRMS, operated by NASA's ESDIS at the Goddard Space Flight Center.
